name: Mission Beach
tagline: Four beach villages on 14 km of golden sand, ringed by World Heritage rainforest
description: Mission Beach is a string of four beach villages on the Cassowary Coast, about halfway between Townsville and Cairns. Wide golden sand backs onto lowland rainforest where the endangered southern cassowary still roams. Offshore, Dunk Island and the Family Islands sit in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park. Galleries, cafes and small resorts sit between the palms and the forest edge.

goodToKnow.title: Stinger season swims
goodToKnow.detail: Marine stingers are present from about November to May. Swim only in stinger-net areas or wear a full-body stinger suit.

goodToKnow.title: Drive slowly for cassowaries
goodToKnow.detail: Cassowaries cross roads in the rainforest and have been hit by cars. Keep to the speed limit, and never feed or approach one.

goodToKnow.title: Base between Cairns and Townsville
goodToKnow.detail: The village is a 26 km detour off the Bruce Highway near Tully, or 16 km from El Arish. Buses stop at Wongaling Beach.

name: Port Douglas
tagline: A palm-lined resort town where the Great Barrier Reef meets the Daintree
description: Port Douglas is a small resort town about an hour north of Cairns, with a village feel and palm trees taller than the buildings. Four Mile Beach runs along its front, and Macrossan Street is lined with cafes, pubs and restaurants. It is a base for reef trips and for the Daintree Rainforest, with Cape Tribulation a 90-minute drive on sealed roads. Wildlife parks and Mossman Gorge sit close by.
whyVisit: Sail out to the Great Barrier Reef
Stroll Four Mile Beach at sunset
Meet crocodiles and cassowaries at wildlife parks

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles on the beach
goodToKnow.detail: Saltwater crocodiles live here. Heed warning signs on Four Mile Beach, avoid the water's edge at dusk, and stay out if it is closed.

goodToKnow.title: Stinger season Nov to May
goodToKnow.detail: Swim in the netted, lifeguard-patrolled area at the north end of Four Mile Beach, and check the day's stinger risk sign.

goodToKnow.title: Cairns is the gateway
goodToKnow.detail: The airport is in Cairns, one hour south on the winding Captain Cook Highway. Shuttles run from the airport, and tours pick up at hotels.

bestTimeBlurb: Peak season is {months}, the dry months, with sunny days and no stinger season.

name: Daintree
tagline: Ancient World Heritage rainforest that meets the Great Barrier Reef at the shore
description: The Daintree is a tropical rainforest in Far North Queensland, thought to be over 135 million years old and part of the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area. It is one of the few places where two World Heritage sites, the rainforest and the Great Barrier Reef, meet. Visitors cross the Daintree River by cable ferry to reach Cape Tribulation and its beaches, boardwalks and wildlife. The cassowary is its icon, alongside about 430 bird species.

goodToKnow.title: Cross by cable ferry
goodToKnow.detail: The Daintree River Ferry takes you north to Cape Tribulation. Fares (Sep 2025) were $31 one-way and $51 return per car.

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and stingers
goodToKnow.detail: Crocodiles live in the river, creeks and sea, and stingers are present in summer. Stay away from the shore and never swim at night.

goodToKnow.title: Avoid the wet season
goodToKnow.detail: November to March is the rainy and cyclone season. Check road conditions before heading north of the river.

bestTimeBlurb: Go in {months}, the drier months, for easier walking. Summer brings heavy rain and cyclones.

name: Cooktown
tagline: A frontier port where Captain Cook beached the Endeavour, gateway to Cape York
description: Cooktown is a small coastal town on the Endeavour River estuary, where Captain Cook beached his ship for 48 days in 1770. A century later it was the port for the Palmer River goldfields, and grand buildings from that boom remain. The town has a frontier feel, far from the resort towns further south. Grassy Hill, waterfalls and rainforest sit around it, and it is the base for travel north into Cape York.
whyVisit: Climb Grassy Hill for sweeping views

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and stingers
goodToKnow.detail: Crocodiles have been sighted at Finch Bay and Cherry Tree Bay, and stingers are present in season. Do not wade in creeks or the sea.

goodToKnow.title: Wet season road closures
goodToKnow.detail: Roads north can close quickly as creeks rise at crossings. Check conditions before driving, and never cross a flooded creek.

bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, the dry season, for warm, less humid days. The wet season runs December to April.

name: Winton
tagline: The outback town where Waltzing Matilda was first sung and dinosaurs roamed
description: Winton is a small outback town between Longreach and Mount Isa. It is where Waltzing Matilda was first performed in 1895, and it was the first headquarters of the company that became Qantas. The surrounding country is rich in dinosaur fossils, including Australovenator, which is named for the town. Quirky stops such as Arno's Wall and the Musical Fence add to the outback character.
whyVisit: Learn the story of Waltzing Matilda

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat
goodToKnow.detail: Summer days often reach 40°C. Visitor season runs April to October, and tours and experiences are reduced outside it.

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: There is no public transport in town and the nearest hire cars are in Longreach, about two hours away. The dinosaur sites involve unsealed roads.

bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, when the outback is milder and tours run. Summer is harsh, with days often reaching 40°C.
